adminBackup.pageSubtitle: Restore only current balances, inventory, reservations, and open obligations to the same guild workspace. Template sharing and Discord server transfers are separate.
adminBackup.recoveryExportHint: Save the current state needed for incident recovery as JSON with an integrity hash and source guild identity.

adminBackup.excludedItems: Settings, permissions, templates, future events, closed history, full ledger history, statistics, notifications, caches, and Discord server transfer

adminBackup.templateHint: Share only event and slot configurations. Member, financial, ledger, and inventory data cannot appear in this file format.
adminBackup.templateSafetyNote: Templates with the same name are updated; all other templates remain unchanged.
adminBackup.recentReceiptsHint: Successful atomic recoveries and their server-side safety snapshots.

quickStart.title: First-time setup — 7-step checklist
quickStart.intro: Just installed the bot? Walk through these 7 steps in order before launching. Skipping any of them tends to break other features later.
quickStart.step1: Discord bot install — happens automatically when you sign up. If the bot is missing or under-permissioned, re-invite from albion-guildmanager.com/invite.
quickStart.step2: Set the Albion home guild — Settings → Guild tab, search for your guild name, and link it. This anchors verification, killboard, and stats, so do this first.
quickStart.step3: Pick the operating timezone — same screen. Choose KR (KST) / EU (CET·CEST) / NA (EST·EDT) / SA (BRT) based on where most of your members live.
quickStart.step4: Configure admin roles — Settings → Permissions tab. Pick at least one Discord role that should grant admin access. Confirm one of your own roles is in the list.
quickStart.step5: Wire up the notification channel and role — Settings → Events tab. Choose the Discord channel where events get posted and the role to mention. Without this, the channel-announce button silently fails.
quickStart.step6: Run a tiny test event — create a small dry-run event and walk through publish → notify → bulk-payout once. Future operations go smoothly after this rehearsal.
quickStart.step7: Invite your members — share the site URL (or albion-guildmanager.com/invite) and ask new members to verify their Albion nickname through the onboarding modal.

roleLoops.title: Role-based operating loops
roleLoops.intro: Each officer should operate from their own work area. Do not place large task blocks inside member-facing pages; keep summaries in the top status chip and approval badges.
roleLoops.eventLead: Event lead: finish recruiting, party edits, announcements, and bulk rewards from Event admin, then open supply or finance pages only when needed.
roleLoops.regearOfficer: Regear officer: mainly watch the Regear tab in Approvals and regear windows. Exchange and donation reviews require separate finance approval permissions.
roleLoops.financeOfficer: Finance officer: review Exchange / Donation tabs in Approvals and check Stats. Regear price edits or inventory delivery still require separate permissions.
roleLoops.supplyOfficer: Supply officer: run Guild shop, Guild inventory, Loot audit, and Craft regear. Use each feature page's filters and badges for member requests.
roleLoops.analyst: Analyst: review Battles, Stats, and Audit log to support operations. This can stay read-heavy without granting mutation permissions.

eventLifecycle.title: Event lifecycle
eventLifecycle.step1: Create event: fill in time/location/notes. Saved as draft initially.
eventLifecycle.step2: Configure parties/slots: load a template or add parties → set role, gear, and spec per slot.
eventLifecycle.step3: Publish: use the banner button to move the event to a state where members can apply.
eventLifecycle.step4: Operational start: published events start automatically at gather time, locking the roster and policy. You do not need to record the actual combat start.
eventLifecycle.step5: After the event: the auto-regear job reads killboard and generates approvals. Members can submit manual regear once the window opens. Use the 'Bulk payout' button at the top of the event page to grant a fixed attendance point to every assigned member in one click.

regear.title: Regear system
regear.body: Three regear modes coexist: auto (killboard-based), event-tied manual (screenshot-based), and 'regear windows' (event-independent open intake). Setting the per-role reward cap to 0 blocks all regear claims from that role.
regear.bullet1: The auto-regear toggle is a global switch. It must be ON for killboard deaths to be converted into approvals automatically.
regear.bullet2: Slot editor has 'Exclude from auto-regear' (visible only when global ON) and 'Exclude from manual regear' (always) checkboxes for per-build opt-out.
regear.bullet3: Event-tied manual regear opens after the configured delay from operational start. Max screenshot 10MB, PNG/JPEG/WebP only.
regear.bullet4: Auto-generated pending rows let the claimant edit per-slot prices. Admins review at /admin/dashboard/regear.
regear.bullet5: Event-independent free regear is accepted via 'regear windows'. Open and close them at /admin/dashboard/regear-windows (or via the admin-only button on the top right of /regear) — set a title, deadline, and per-user cap. The deadline uses the same 4-part (month/day/hour/minute) input as events for mobile-friendly entry.

craftRegear.title: Crafted regear (guild boxes)
craftRegear.body: Crafted regear is a guild-wide payout mode for new regear claims. Off creates new claims as silver; on creates them as craft candidates. During admin review, officers finish each claim as a silver payout, a craft-queue task, or a stock issue. Crafted payouts then show the requester a pickup box on My craft pickups. Multiple parts for the same requester share the same box.
craftRegear.bullet1: In Admin → Craft regear, grant 'Crafter' permission to selected members. Only crafters can claim queued tasks.
craftRegear.bullet2: Assign each crafter a 'box range' (e.g., 1-10). The server blocks overlapping ranges between crafters automatically. Without a range, auto-assign is disabled and the crafter must enter a number manually.
craftRegear.bullet3: When a crafter opens the Deliver dialog, the system picks a box automatically: (1) reuse the same box if the requester already has one in use, otherwise (2) the smallest free number in the crafter's range. The crafter can override manually.
craftRegear.bullet4: A box only frees up once the requester collects (or it expires). Multiple parts may stack in the same box, so remind requesters to collect everything in a single trip.
craftRegear.bullet5: Per-role caps, the global box-number range (1-999), expiry days, and focus bonus all live in the 'Settings' card at the top. The 'Active tasks' panel below shows every task in flight; admins can force-cancel or convert to silver from there.

onboarding.title: Albion nickname verification
onboarding.body:
New members see an Albion server/nickname onboarding modal after login. On successful verification, both the site and Discord guild nicknames sync to the Albion name.

Verification requires an 'Albion home guild ID' set in Settings → Guild tab. Without it, identities are stored but left unverified (verifiedAt=null).

A single Albion home guild can only belong to one site at a time — if another site has already claimed the same guild, that one must release it before you can verify here. During initial setup, choosing the home guild also auto-syncs the subdomain slug to the guild name. Changing the home guild later does NOT rename the subdomain.

The Stats page shows unverified/pending members. The 'Re-onboard' button clears a member's albion_* fields so the modal shows again.

timezone.title: Operating timezone
timezone.body:
The site-wide reference timezone for displaying and entering all times. During initial setup, pick KR (KST) / EU (CET·CEST) / NA (EST·EDT) / SA (BRT). All gather times, operational starts, regear deadlines, and stats follow this zone.

The same timezone drives auto-regear day boundaries, the 'today/this week' grouping in stats, and the 35-min Discord DM alert. Setting it to where the majority of your members live cuts down on "what time is that?" confusion.

You can change it any time in Settings → Guild tab. Stored absolute timestamps stay the same — only how they're displayed changes.

bombSquad.title: Bomb-squad party & caller
bombSquad.body:
Bomb-squad parties use a 'members apply freely → caller approves/direct-assigns' flow. To use it:

1) Go to Settings → Permissions and configure at least one caller role.
2) Have at least one guild member with that role.
3) In the event party editor, toggle 'Bomb Squad' on and pick a caller.

Callers manage their own party's slots and members directly from a dedicated edit page.

shop.title: Guild shop
shop.body:
Members exchange points they earned for gear. Stock syncs by copying and pasting the Albion log into the import form.

The 'exchange / discount rate' converts silver prices into point prices. 100% means silver price equals point price; 50% sells at half price.

When item prices diverge sharply from current market or look unusual, an automatic warning appears. Review and adjust those rows manually.

siphon.title: Siphon ledger
siphon.body: Paste in-game siphon deposit/withdraw logs to calculate each member's balance. Set the official accounting start on the siphon admin page (or Settings → Guild), and if the ledger gets polluted, reset the raw siphon logs from the same page before importing again.

lootAudit.title: Loot log audit
lootAudit.body: Compare post-ZvZ personal loot CSVs with guild chest deposit logs to find suspected missing returns. The first loot timestamp in each audit becomes the reference point, and only guild chest deposit rows before that time are excluded.

notifications.title: Discord notifications
notifications.body:
Notifications are delivered three ways:

- Channel announcement: posted to the event channel with a role mention. Goes out only when you press the manual button after creating or editing an event.
- Personal DM: auto-sent to assigned members before the event gather time. The lead time follows the guild default (initially 35 min, configurable in the Events tab → Event notifications); each member can override it in 'My settings', or opt out entirely. Approval / rejection of regear or point exchange also triggers a DM to the requester.
- Admin operations alerts: pending approvals, shop orders, craft deliveries, sync delays, and unverified members can be sent to a separate admin-only channel. Configure topics, mention roles, and 30 min / 1 h / 3 h / daily digest intervals.

This requires the Discord bot, notification channels, roles, and permissions to be configured first. After a fresh bot invite, check Settings → Events/Notifications for the channel and role mappings.

battles.title: Battle records (auto-aggregated)
battles.body: Guild battles are pulled from the Albion API every 5 minutes, then direct K/D events are interpreted as actual engagements. Until the source and events are stable, the system shows collecting, segmentation required, or insufficient evidence instead of inventing a result. The full rules are under 'Show classification rules' on the battle records page.
battles.bullet1: Even within one Albion battle, a fight that stops and later restarts becomes a separate engagement. Gaps up to 2 minutes stay together, gaps of 8 minutes or more split, and the interval between them requires segmentation review.
battles.bullet2: An official result requires at least 20 players on our side and at least 20 combined players across non-intervention opponents. Sub-20 opponents remain separate 1:N matchups when their combined size qualifies.
battles.bullet3: An advantage or disadvantage requires at least 5 eligible direct events, with both K/D and kill fame leading in the same direction by at least 20%. Everything else is close or pending.
battles.bullet4: Several opponents in one continuous flow produce one engagement result with per-opponent evidence. A one-event secondary opponent is marked as an intervention and excluded from the result.

stats.title: Stats & monitoring
stats.body: Top/bottom point holders, event participation, shop/regear activity, and Albion verification status in one page. Use the inline 'Re-onboard' button to restart the onboarding flow for unverified members.

tips.title: Operation tips
tips.tip1: Before major changes, review feature states and global toggles such as auto-regear. Gather-time operational start is always enforced.
tips.tip2: Save your common party layouts as templates so you can reuse them when building events. Re-saving with the same name prompts whether to overwrite the existing template.
tips.tip3: Use the party editor's 'Hide party' button to hide work-in-progress parties from members.
tips.tip4: If unexplained errors keep happening, first check bot permissions, channel settings, and the home guild setting, then share the details with your site admin.
tips.tip5: Share albion-guildmanager.com/invite as a one-click bot install link with your guild — it lands directly on the Discord bot invite page.
tips.tip6: Event gather time and regear-window deadlines now use the same 4-part (month/day/hour/minute) inputs everywhere, so mobile keypads stay consistent. Times convert to your operating timezone automatically.
tips.tip7: Reminder DMs use a guild-wide default (Settings → Events → Event notifications), and members can override their personal lead time anywhere from 5 to 1440 minutes in /me/settings. Useful when commute schedules differ across the roster.

troubleshooting.title: Troubleshooting
troubleshooting.intro: Common issues and how to fix them. If you're still stuck, check Discord bot permissions and server settings first, then contact your site admin.
troubleshooting.p1Title: A member can't verify their Albion nickname
troubleshooting.p1Body: Make sure the 'Albion home guild' is set in Settings → Guild tab — verification won't complete without it. If another site has already claimed the same Albion guild as its home, that one needs to release it first.
troubleshooting.p2Body: Confirm the home guild and the Albion server (Americas / Europe / Asia) match. The Albion API polls every 5 minutes, so kills from the last 5–10 minutes appear shortly after. Kills from unverified members may also be missing from aggregates.
troubleshooting.p3Body: Check that the global 'auto-regear' toggle is ON in Settings → Regear, the per-slot 'Exclude from auto-regear' is OFF, and the per-role cap isn't 0. Auto-regear only recognizes Black Zone deaths and always creates rows in the 'pending' state — admins must approve before payout.
troubleshooting.p4Body: Channel announcements require the channel and role to be set in Settings → Events, plus a manual 'send announcement' click after publishing. Personal DMs only arrive when the bot is in the same Discord server as the member and the member hasn't disabled notifications in /me/settings.
troubleshooting.p5Title: Battles aren't showing up in records
troubleshooting.p5Body: An encounter is excluded from official results when our side or the combined non-intervention opponents has fewer than 20 players. Low-engagement events (scouting, retreats) where K+D is far below team size are also filtered. The full ruleset is behind 'Show classification rules' on the battles page.
troubleshooting.p6Body: First confirm they're logging in with their own Discord account and are members of a Discord server the bot is in. If they aren't recognized as admin, verify the admin role configured in Settings → Permissions is actually granted to them.
troubleshooting.p7Body: 'Exchange / discount rate' converts silver to points: 100% means silver-equals-points, 50% means half-price. Large divergence from market triggers an automatic warning. Market price refresh can lag, so re-check after a few minutes.

adminRegearMode.silverHint: Process approved amounts through the points and silver payout flow.
adminRegearMode.craftedHint: Crafters deliver finished items to rotating pickup boxes.
adminRegearMode.autoHint: After events end, auto-creates pending claims by reading killboard deaths and pricing them at current market rates. Off = manual claims only.

adminShopImport.title: Guild chest log sync
adminShopImport.description: Copy the latest section of the in-game guild chest log, then let the site apply only the new confirmed rows to stock. Pasting does not change stock; the public shop updates only after you review the result and apply it.
adminShopImport.syncGuideTitle: How should I paste the log?
adminShopImport.syncGuideStepCopy: 1. Copy the latest section from the in-game guild chest log.
adminShopImport.syncGuideStepCheck: 2. Include a few rows that overlap with the site's last applied log when possible.
adminShopImport.syncGuideStepApply: 3. When the site ignores duplicates and shows only new rows, apply them to stock.
adminShopImport.syncGuideOverlapHint: Overlapping is safe. It helps the site confirm the handoff point and detect missing middle sections.
adminShopImport.checkpointEmpty: No guild chest log has been saved yet. For first-time setup, confirm a current stock baseline first if possible.
adminShopImport.firstImportHint: If this is your first guild chest import, incomplete historical logs can distort inventory. Use "Inventory baseline" first to lock the current chest stock, then accumulate only new logs from that point.
adminShopImport.placeholder:
Paste copied text from the in-game "Bank" log. Example:
"04/21/2026 15:59:10"	"SoonSem"	"Lightning Coil"	"0"	"1"	"-1"
"04/21/2026 13:42:13"	"WarGloves"	"Cleric Robe"	"1"	"2"	"1"
adminShopImport.resolveBeforeCommit: Blacklist unresolved items or remove their batches before applying inventory changes.
adminShopImport.fileReadFail: Failed to read file — drop a .txt or .rtf file.

adminShopImport.stagingBackfillBody: There are no new rows after the site's latest record {when}{tail}, but this older pasted range contains {count} saveable rows. Confirm this is an intentional missing-range backfill.

adminShopImport.stagingContinuedBody: {count} new rows were detected after the site's last applied log {when}{tail}. Ready to apply to stock.

adminShopImport.stagingGapWarnBody: No logs for {gap} after the site's last applied log {when}{tail} in this batch. If transactions happened in the gap, stock will be out of sync with reality.

publicCurrentContract.title: The operating rules the app follows today
publicCurrentContract.lead: This is not marketing copy. It is the current contract for user flows and boundaries: which state members and operators share, and who owns the next action, expressed consistently in four languages.
publicCurrentContract.behaviorLead: Features are not isolated menus. Each one shares state with the steps before and after it.

identity.title: Identity and membership history
identity.body: One Discord user may belong to multiple guilds, while one character with the same official server and player ID can be active in only one guild at a time. Where enabled, a limited local account lets Discord-sensitive guests enter event and regear flows.

events.title: Events and actual attendance
events.body: External party members can sign up through a public invite. Signups remain a plan; after the event, an operator confirms actual attendance. The app does not require someone to press an unknowable fight-start button.

regear.title: Regear is separate from participation rewards
regear.body: Regear supports lost equipment after a death; rewards can be granted for actual attendance alone. Every guild chooses unsupported or supported, and only supporting guilds configure silver or crafted fulfillment.

fulfillment.title: Craft delivery and finished inventory
fulfillment.body: Raw materials are not tracked. Finished inventory is deducted only when a crafter places an item in the requester’s box, and guild-funded crafting can use a zero-fee policy.

economy.title: Points, shop, and financial records
economy.body: Point and silver ownership remains in ledgers. Deposits can be observed but their purpose is never guessed automatically, and payout flows remain separate from guilds that only keep records.

inboxes.title: Member requests and operator work
inboxes.body: Members see action required, waiting on guild, and history in one inbox that deep-links to each source. Operators see approvals, payouts, and crafting from one snapshot without duplicate counting.

menhera.title: Menhera video gate and achievements
menhera.body: Attendance, regear, and point earning work without video, but exchange remains blocked until one video is verified. Achievements include both consistent participation and independently verifiable combat performance.

preferences.title: Language, timezone, and multiple guilds
preferences.body: Language and timezone follow the Discord access identity across guilds. Guild roles, permissions, membership history, and operational data remain isolated inside each tenant.

publicCurrentContract.featureStatesLead: Navigation, direct URLs, server actions, Discord commands, and automation obey the same state rules.

disabled.label: Disabled
disabled.body: New intake and automation stop and navigation is hidden. Existing records remain read-only where they must be preserved.

setupRequired.label: Setup required
setupRequired.body: Only required setup is available before launch; real intake and processing remain blocked.

enabled.body: Reading, new intake, processing, notifications, and automation are all available.

draining.body: New intake and automation stop while existing requests can still be read, completed, and notified where necessary.

publicCurrentContract.honestyTitle: We do not productize judgments the app cannot make reliably
publicCurrentContract.honestyBody: Because the app cannot accurately judge what was tactically good or bad in Albion, automated tactical grading and narrative post-fight reports are excluded from the core product. It shows source records and verifiable operational state instead.

publicFeatures.pageSubtitle: Automate the core guild workflow first
publicFeatures.pageLead: Clean ZvZ analytics, event/build signup, and member self-service come first. Regear, shop, and craft tools are review-based automation layered on top.
publicFeatures.f1Body: Build parties and slots, publish, and the bot pushes an @everyone alert to your channel. Members sign up for slots on the web and check in for attendance.
publicFeatures.f2Body: Killboard syncs every 5 minutes to find candidate deaths, then AODP market data prepares a draft claim. Final payout is confirmed only after claimant review and admin approval.
publicFeatures.f2Bullet1: 5-minute killboard candidates + AODP pricing from your primary city
publicFeatures.f2Bullet2: Per-slot price edit, re-issue, reject workflow
publicFeatures.f2Bullet3: Blackzone-only · claimant review + admin approval (two-stage) · global off toggle
publicFeatures.f3Body: Run an internal shop where regear / event points buy in-game items. Exchange rate equals discount — silver and points are 1:1, so the math stays intuitive.
publicFeatures.f4Title: ZvZ Analytics — discover your members' true specialties
publicFeatures.f4Body: Other Albion tools just dump raw killboards. We extract real ZvZ only — auto-filtering ganks and low-engagement fights, counting only records after a member joins. The result: per-member weapon-category specialty, matchup-by-matchup guild records, attendance, and survival rate.
publicFeatures.f4Bullet1: Matchup-level guild records — N–M against this guild
publicFeatures.f4Bullet2: Per-member weapon category specialty + K/D + survival rate
publicFeatures.f4Bullet3: Clean ZvZ-filtered data (20 players per side for official fights)
publicFeatures.f5Body: When the guild enables crafted regear, new claims are created as craft candidates. Admins finish each claim during review as silver payout, craft-queue task, or stock issue; crafters then build the gear and deliver it to pickup boxes.
publicFeatures.f5Bullet2: Review-time choice: silver payout / craft queue / stock issue
publicFeatures.f6Title: Build-sheet recruitment — reusable ZvZ gear in one click
publicFeatures.f6Body: Large ZvZ events repeat the same locus, tank, and Engage DPS builds over and over. Officers prepare build sheets once, then apply them from an image-first palette inside the event editor.
publicFeatures.f6Bullet1: Save build sheets by role and category
publicFeatures.f6Bullet2: Pick from gear-image cards instead of text-only rows

publicFaq.pageLead: Before installing, here are the questions guild leaders usually ask about permissions, data, pricing, and auto-regear rules.
publicFaq.q1: What Discord permissions does the bot need?
publicFaq.a1: Anyone with Manage Server permission can install. The bot uses only message-send, member-read, and role-read scopes.
publicFaq.q2: How does it pull Albion guild data?
publicFaq.a2: We pull Albion's official data every 5 minutes to refresh kill records. Loss values come from AODP (Albion Online Data Project) — a public dataset where players share market prices they collect in-game.
publicFaq.a3: All features are free during the beta period before the full release.
publicFaq.a4: In a secure cloud database. Guilds are isolated, so no other guild can read your data. Data from an explicitly deleted guild is permanently cleaned up only after a 30-day grace period.
publicFaq.a5: All official servers — Americas, Europe, and Asia. Pick your server during onboarding and the bot uses that server's kill records and price data.
publicFaq.q6: Can I delegate admin to other members?
publicFaq.a6: Yes. Admin is granted by Discord role: anyone with the configured admin role is automatically an admin on the site.
publicFaq.a7: Each Discord server maps to one guild workspace. The same Discord user can join or operate multiple guilds and switch workspaces from the My Guilds menu.
publicFaq.q8: What happens if my guild stops using it?
publicFaq.a8: Guilds with no admin login for 30+ days are flagged inactive. After further inactivity we may suspend with notice (data preserved).
publicFaq.a9: The default sign-in is Discord OAuth. If a guild enables Albion account entry, only a hash of the site-only password is stored; we never ask for Discord passwords or Albion game credentials. All traffic is encrypted, and data is isolated per guild.
publicFaq.q10: How do I fully delete my guild from the site?
publicFaq.a10: An officer with the dedicated workspace-deletion permission must first resolve open payouts, trades, crafting work, and other obligations, then reauthenticate with Discord, enter the exact guild name, and confirm. The request can be cancelled from the same screen for 30 days; after that, the guild's product data and files are permanently deleted.
publicFaq.q11: How is this different from other Albion tools (Battle Tabs, standalone Discord bots, etc.)?
publicFaq.a11: Event ops (party building, DM reminders, attendance points), reward automation (auto regear, guild shop, point exchange), and ZvZ stats are unified in one site, so you don't need spreadsheets or multiple Discord bots. We pull from Discord and the Albion kill records directly, so manual input is minimal.
publicFaq.q12: Aren't the bot's permissions too broad?
publicFaq.a12: The bot uses only message-send, member/role read, and DM-send. It doesn't read message content or touch voice channels. If permissions feel too broad, an admin can further constrain the bot role directly from Discord server settings.
publicFaq.q13: What should I do first after installing the bot?
publicFaq.a13: 1) Sign in with Discord after inviting the bot, 2) set your guild's address, 3) pick your Albion home guild, 4) assign the event-announcement channel and the active-member role, 5) review operating policies like auto-regear and the guild shop — once these five are done, members can sign in and link their Albion characters.
publicFaq.q14: What does a member do the first time they visit the site?
publicFaq.a14: Signing in with Discord starts the verification flow automatically. Enter your Albion character name to match the guild roster — once verified, your kill log, claims, and reward points start accumulating automatically. Entering a character that isn't on the guild roster leaves you in [unverified] state and some features will be limited.
publicFaq.q15: My death isn't getting picked up by auto-regear. Why?
publicFaq.a15: 1) Albion's kill records take about 30 minutes to appear in the official feed after a death — wait a moment and press 'Recheck' on the regear page. 2) Auto-regear only catches deaths in the black zone. Yellow/red-zone or non-ZvZ deaths must be submitted manually. 3) Make sure your Albion character is verified and that your guild matches the site's home guild.
publicFaq.q16: How do I customize my guild’s public page?
publicFaq.a16: Admins can edit the `/g/your-guild` page directly — banner image, banner opacity, accent color, description, recruitment status, Discord invite link, active hours, and supported languages. You can also toggle individual sections on or off (member count, battle records, weapon mix, rival guilds, admin team, and more). Use the "Edit banner" button at the top of the public page, or open the public profile settings in the admin panel.
publicFaq.q17: Which languages does the site support?
publicFaq.a17: The site UI ships in Korean, Japanese, English, and Simplified Chinese. Switch language from the top-right language menu and every page updates immediately. Note that the documentation pages (`/docs`) themselves are currently Korean-only; translations are in progress.
publicFaq.q18: The public page shows the Albion English guild name. Can I show our Discord name instead?
publicFaq.a18: The public page (`/g/your-guild`) and SEO metadata always prefer your in-game Albion guild name (English) — Albion only permits English characters in guild names, and matching that name keeps the page consistent with how other players search for you or track you on the killboard. The localized Discord name is only used inside admin surfaces. To change your home guild after first setup, contact the operator (super-admin).
publicFaq.ctaTitle: Still unsure? Start with the demo.
publicFaq.ctaBody: Read the docs to understand the rules, then use the demo to see how member and admin screens connect.

battleTracking.tipMatch: This view preserves Albion battle originals as a ledger and renders a separate guild-facing observation view.
battleTracking.tipEngagement: The default tab shows engagements with direct guild events, at least 20 players on our side, and at least 20 combined non-intervention opponents. Smaller battles still retain their source record.
battleTracking.tipOutcome: An engagement is an advantage or disadvantage only when direct K/D and kill fame each differ by at least 20% in the same direction; otherwise it is close or pending.
battleTracking.tipLimitation: When event flow cannot establish a reliable boundary, the system leaves it as "Engagement boundary unclear" instead of forcing a split.
battleTracking.rulesIntro: This page preserves source battles and interprets their event flow as engagements. Stats, achievements, and regear use only verified official engagements and their result-eligible events.
battleTracking.rule1Body: Direct means your guild appears in the battle original. Alliance means your guild is absent, but a guild in the same alliance at battle time appears.
battleTracking.rule2Intro: The size category uses whichever is larger: the allied side at battle time or the combined result-eligible opponent forces. Force size is only a battle condition and never changes the result.
battleTracking.rule2CutOff: The allied side must have at least 20 players, and non-intervention opponent forces must total at least 20. Individual forces may be smaller than 20; they remain separate 1:N matchups instead of being merged into a fabricated coalition.
battleTracking.rule3Body: Direct K/D events establish an engagement. Kills or deaths from only one side still count as engagement evidence, but fewer than five result-eligible events keeps the result and result-based statistics pending.
battleTracking.rule3Why: Why? A single intervention, stragglers, or incomplete collection must not flip win rate or achievements. Nothing is deleted; factual evidence and the judgment state remain visible.
battleTracking.rule4Body: There must be at least five result-eligible direct events. K/D and kill-fame ratios must both lead in the same direction by at least 20% for advantage/disadvantage; conflicting directions or either margin below 20% is a close fight.
battleTracking.rule5Body: When several opponents appear in one continuous fight, the engagement receives one result while K/D and kill fame stay broken down per opponent. A second opponent with exactly one event is marked as an intervention and excluded from the result.
battleTracking.rule6Body: A result requires two consecutive identical source snapshots and exact source-vs-event K/D reconciliation. Events within two minutes stay together, an eight-minute gap clearly splits engagements, and the interval between them remains boundary-unclear.
battleTracking.rulesLimit1: Final-blow logs cannot reveal formation, calls, or actual front-line movement. Ambiguous time boundaries are therefore excluded from official results and result-based statistics.
battleTracking.rulesLimit2: Only battles exposed via Albion's public API are tracked. Private skirmishes (small non-ZvZ ganks, etc.) are not aggregated.

shop.aodpTooltip: Market prices come from AODP (Albion Online Data Project) — a public dataset where players share market prices they capture from the game. Data density varies by server, city, and time, so when recent prices aren't available for the configured base city, the system falls back through lower quality → 14-day average → other royal cities → red-zone cities. When that fallback chain runs, the estimate may diverge from real trade value, and a "Price estimate" warning is shown.

priceWarningBuyer.quality: Price estimate: no market data for this item quality, so we substituted a lower-quality price.
priceWarningBuyer.window: Price estimate: recent market data is sparse, averaged over up to 14 days.
priceWarningBuyer.bluezone: Price estimate: no price data for the current city, so we used another Royal City's price. Actual trades may incur teleport cost and travel time.
priceWarningBuyer.redzone: Price estimate: no Royal City data at all — we used Red Zone prices (Caerleon / Brecilien). Actual value may differ significantly due to PvP risk.

priceWarningAdmin.quality: Price estimate: no data for the requested quality, so we substituted a lower-quality price.

adminSiphonPage.resetConfirm: Delete all siphon logs for the current guild? Per-member siphon balances will recalculate to zero. This cannot be undone. Continue?
adminSiphonPage.resetTargetEmpty: There are no siphon logs to delete.
adminSiphonPage.resetTargetUnknown: Could not confirm the delete target count. Check permissions and network status before continuing.
adminSiphonPage.emptyState: No siphon logs yet. Paste an in-game log above to start.

adminSiphonPage.activityDescription: Deposits and withdrawals are activity totals only. Sorting and totals are not debt or enforcement criteria.

adminLootAuditPage.previewStale: The input changed after analysis. Analyze it again before saving.
adminLootAuditPage.parseWarnings: Some rows could not be parsed.
adminLootAuditPage.parseErrorReasonLootMissingHeaders: The loot CSV is missing required headers. Check timestamp_utc, looted_by__name, item_id, item_name, and quantity.

adminLootAuditPage.parseErrorReasonLootRequiredFields: Looter, item ID, or item name is empty.

adminLootAuditPage.parseErrorReasonLootMarketValue: Estimated market value must be a non-negative integer.
adminLootAuditPage.parseErrorReasonChestFormat: The chest log must have 6 columns: date, player, item, enchantment, quality, and quantity.
adminLootAuditPage.parseErrorReasonChestDate: The chest-log date could not be read.
adminLootAuditPage.parseErrorReasonChestNumericFields: Chest-log enchantment, quality, and quantity must be numeric.

adminLootAuditPage.itemCheckDescription: If the same item ID was deposited in total, it is treated as returned even when the looter and depositor differ.

home.introBody: Review the public profile, admin queue, member dashboard, battle tracking, and weapon analytics flow.
home.step1Body: Recruitment status, alliance and timezone surfaced instantly. The same page used for Discord shares and SEO indexing.
home.step2Body: Regear, exchange, point top-up, shop, payout, and craft requests collected into one card. No more channel hopping.
home.step3Body: Once Discord + Albion are linked, members see their own K/D, attendance, and regear history in one view. No more payout disputes.
home.step4Body: Events, wins/losses, and K/D refresh automatically. Guild trends visible without spreadsheets.
home.step5Body: Only the ZvZ battles your guild joined are auto-classified, with K/D and matchup labelled automatically. No need to dig through the killboard.
home.step6Body: Weapon category distribution gives evidence-based build decisions.
home.completedBody: Now explore Events, Members, Settings, and Core state recovery from the sidebar.

events.introBody: Walk through the same order as the real admin home: required setup, today's work, invite link, and event list.
events.step1Body: Confirm the items needed before operations, such as announcement channels, home guild, and public profile settings.
events.step2Body: Pending approvals, required setup, sync health, and member verification are summarized as cards.
events.step3Body: Copy the URL new guild members use to start Discord login and Albion verification.
events.step4Body: This is the entry point for creating and publishing upcoming ZvZ events for guild-wide announcements.
events.step5Body: Recurring meetups become templates once, then seed the next event when needed.
events.step6Body: Each event card manages participants, weapon/gear slot assignments, and the schedule in one place.
events.completedBody: The demo now follows the real operations home from today's work through event publishing.

builds.introBody: See how reusable ZvZ gear builds are saved and then loaded from the event editor palette.
builds.step1Body: Officers create new builds and search existing builds from here.
builds.step2Body: Find similar gear sets by role or build name before editing an event.
builds.step3Body: Weapon and armor icons make similar builds easier to distinguish than text-only rows.
builds.completedBody: In the real event editor, these build cards feed directly into the slot palette.

regear.introBody: Walk through the unified queue for regear, exchanges, point top-ups, shop orders, payouts, and craft work.
regear.step1Body: Regear, exchange, point top-up, shop order, payout, craft — every admin approval funneled into one page. Badges show pending counts.
regear.step2Body: Auto regear is generated by cron from the killboard; manual is filed by members. Filter them separately to review.
regear.step3Body: Each regear card lets you adjust per-slot prices (head/chest/hands/feet/weapon/shield/mount). Claimants tune to current market.
regear.completedBody: Other approval type tabs (exchange/point top-up/shop) follow the same flow.

members.introBody: Review member status, tab grouping, and member detail navigation.
members.step1Body: Total members + this week's cumulative participation appear directly in the header.
members.step2Body: Members · Roster · Guests · Withdrawn — four tabs separate full members, the roster list, temporary guests, and leavers.
members.completedBody: Click any member row for personal stats and regear history.

stats.introBody: See how point balances, holders, finance flow, and operating metrics are presented.
stats.step1Body: Total held points, lifetime earned/spent, holder count — four KPI cards capture your guild's economy at a glance.
stats.step2Body: Ranked by point balance — instantly spot your most active members, with admin badges marked.
stats.step3Body: Daily earned/spent chart for the last N days + breakdown by source and sink. Track where points come in and go out.
stats.completedBody: Scroll further for verification, event participation, shop & regear stats.

audit.introBody: Track who changed what when disputes or mistakes need review.
audit.step1Body: Action · target kind · admin/target Discord ID · date range. Surface the one entry you need within 30 seconds during a dispute.
audit.step2Body: Who · when · which action · which target. Expand the JSON details to inspect before/after values for any change.
audit.step3Body: Paginated 10 entries per page by default. Total count is always visible at the top.
audit.completedBody: Try changing the filters — picture how you'd use this for disputes inside your own guild.

siphon.introBody: An admin view for pasting in-game siphon deposit and withdrawal logs and tracking each member's Siphoned Energy balance.
siphon.step1Body: Paste the date/player/purpose/quantity log copied from the game. The app calculates deposits and withdrawals.
siphon.step2Body: If a wrong file was saved or old logs were mixed in, delete only this guild's raw siphon logs and import again from the same start point.
siphon.step3Body: See who deposited and who used siphons, with positive and negative balances.
siphon.step4Body: When questions come up, trace the original time, player, quantity, and importing officer.
siphon.completedBody: Admins manage the full ledger; members check only their own siphon balance.

permissions.introBody: Grant non-admin officers only the screens and actions they need.
permissions.step1Body: Review admin roles, event creator roles, and active member roles in one place.
permissions.step2Body: Choose job-based presets such as regear officer, quartermaster, log operations officer, craft lead, or analyst.
permissions.step3Body: Tune role permissions such as regear approval, event creation, inventory management, and stats access.
permissions.step4Body: Grant or revoke permissions for a specific member when role-level rules are not enough.
permissions.completedBody: Guild leaders can delegate work without handing out full admin access.

myRequests.introBody: Members can check their own regear, exchange, and point top-up request statuses in one place.
myRequests.step1Body: Pending and total counts are split by feature.
myRequests.step2Body: Auto and manual regears show whether they are pending, approved, or rejected.
myRequests.step3Body: Point-to-silver exchange requests show amount and handler.
myRequests.step4Body: Silver deposited into the guild bank stays visible as a point-credit request.
myRequests.completedBody: Members can check status before asking admins.

mySiphon.introBody: Members see siphon deposits, withdrawals, and balance for their verified Albion character.
mySiphon.step1Body: Current balance, total deposited, total withdrawn, and latest activity are visible at a glance.

mySiphon.completedBody: Members can self-check siphon balances, reducing admin questions.

publicLegal.privacyIntro: AlbionGuildManager processes only the account, guild, and game-operations data needed to run the service. We do not ask for Albion game passwords or payment information.
publicLegal.privacyDataBody: We store Discord user IDs, display names, avatars, server and role data, Albion character names, guild IDs, event signups, regear claims, shop/points/siphon/craft records, and other data needed for guild operations.
publicLegal.privacyUseBody: We use the data for login, guild-scoped permission checks, event operations, killboard and battle analytics, reward processing, guild shop, craft regear, and audit logs.
publicLegal.privacySharingBody: Guild data is isolated by guild and cannot be viewed by other guilds. Only the fields that a guild admin enables for the public guild page are publicly visible.
publicLegal.privacyRetentionBody: After a guild deletion request, data goes through a recoverable retention period before cleanup. Minimal records may be kept when required for legal obligations or security investigation.
publicLegal.privacyCredentialsBody: We do not collect Albion game passwords, Discord passwords, payment cards, or government identity documents. Default sign-in uses Discord OAuth; optional guild-local Albion account entry stores only a hash of the site-only password.
publicLegal.termsIntro: These terms describe the basic conditions for using the AlbionGuildManager beta. Guild admins are responsible for explaining the service purpose and data use to their members.
publicLegal.termsBetaBody: The service is currently in beta, and features, screens, and policies may change. Any future paid plan will be announced in advance.
publicLegal.termsAdminBody: Guild admins manage Discord roles, site permissions, public-page visibility, and reward policies. Internal disputes caused by incorrect permissions or operational input should be handled by the guild leadership first.
publicLegal.termsGameDataBody: Killboard, market, and battle data are calculated from external public data and guild input, so delays or inaccuracies may occur. Final reward approval and payout remain the guild admin’s responsibility.
publicLegal.termsFairUseBody: Access may be limited if the service is used to scrape other guilds, spam bot notifications, or attempt security bypasses.
publicLegal.termsAvailabilityBody: We work to keep the service stable, but external systems such as Albion official APIs, Discord, Supabase, and Vercel can cause temporary delays or outages.
publicLegal.termsChangesBody: Terms and policies may be updated as the service evolves. Questions and reports are handled through the official Discord channel.
